title: Relative exceptional Hom bijection under a change of compact-support presentation
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\ge1$; put $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Use ordinary constant-$A$ module derived categories on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Write $S_T=\nu_T^*$ for exact derived comparison pullback [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback] and $U_T=R\nu_{T,*}$, with actual unit $\eta_T:1\to U_TS_T$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism, thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism of separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], with compactification $c=(j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X,p_c:\overline X\to Y)$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements] and $\dim\overline X\le d$ for an integer $d\ge0$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Put $F_c=Rp_{c,\mathrm{et},*}j_!^{\mathrm{et}}$, $P_c=Rp_{c,\mathrm{pro},*}j_!^{\mathrm{pro}}$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support, def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. Let $F_c\dashv I_c$ be its specified etale adjunction and $\Phi^c$ its specified bounded etale-origin relative Hom bijection with target functor $S_XI_cU_Y$ [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class, def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Let $F:D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)\to D(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $Q:D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)\to D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ be functors equipped with natural isomorphisms $e:F_c\xrightarrow{\sim}F$, $q:P_c\xrightarrow{\sim}Q$, and an adjunction $F\dashv I$ with Hom bijection $\beta$. Let $r:I_c\xrightarrow{\sim}I$ be the counit-compatible adjunction conjugate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate], characterized by
$$\varepsilon_N\circ F(r_N)=\varepsilon^c_N\circ e_{I_cN}^{-1}.$$
For $G\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $M\in D^+(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ assume $FG\in D^+(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $IU_YM\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. Write $C_{c,G}:P_cS_XG\xrightarrow{\sim}S_YF_cG$ for the canonical comparison at $(G,1)$ [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison, def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness] and set
$$B_G=q_{S_XG}\circ C_{c,G}^{-1}\circ S_Y(e_G^{-1}):S_YFG\xrightarrow{\sim}QS_XG.$$
Then for every $g:QS_XG\to M$ the specified bijection obeys
$$S_X(r_{U_YM})\circ\Phi^c_{G,M}(g\circ q_{S_XG})=S_X\!\left(\beta_{G,U_YM}\!\left(U_Y(g\circ B_G)\circ\eta_{Y,FG}\right)\right).$$
This is an equality of the specified natural Hom bijections after changing both compact-support presentations; its four factors are precomposition with $B_G$, the comparison adjunction, $\beta$, and the fully faithful Hom map of $S_X$. All four factors are bijective on the displayed domains. The identity origin witness contributes no conjugation. No adjunction on arbitrary unbounded pro-etale inputs is asserted.

proof.text: Check the domains of the four factors. Since $G$ is bounded below, the displayed bounded-below comparison functor of [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] places $S_XG$ in $D^+(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$. Thus $(G,1)$ is a witness for a bounded-below pro-etale input, as required for the compact-support comparison. The comparison $C_{c,G}$ is an isomorphism by [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison], with witness $(G,1)$ as in [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness]. Thus $B_G$ is an isomorphism, and precomposition with it is bijective, with inverse precomposition with $B_G^{-1}$. The second factor is the Hom bijection of the specified comparison adjunction $S_Y\dashv U_Y$, sending $b:S_YFG\to M$ to $U_Y(b)\circ\eta_{Y,FG}$. The third is $\beta_{G,U_YM}$, an equivalence on the ordinary etale derived categories by the given adjunction $F\dashv I$. The last is the Hom map of $S_X$, bijective by [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison], because both $G$ and $IU_YM$ are bounded below. For the original presentation, $F_cG$ and $I_cU_YM$ are bounded below as well: they are isomorphic via $e_G$ and $r_{U_YM}$ to $FG$ and $IU_YM$. Here bounded-below categories are strictly full and closed under isomorphisms [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories]. These are precisely the domains required by the original four-factor construction; no pro-etale exceptional adjunction on other objects is used.

source.place: four-factor relative Hom construction and final paragraph on compactification comparisons

proof.text:
Write $N=U_YM$ and let $\beta^c$ denote the Hom bijection of the given etale adjunction $F_c\dashv I_c$. Unpack the specified four-factor construction of $\Phi^c$ at the identity witness: for $h:P_cS_XG\to M$, set
$$a(h)=U_Y(h\circ C_{c,G}^{-1})\circ\eta_{Y,F_cG}:F_cG\to N.$$
Precomposition with $C_{c,G}^{-1}$, the comparison transpose, the etale transpose, and the Hom map of $S_X$ give, respectively,
$$\Phi^c_{G,M}(h)=S_X\bigl(\beta^c_{G,N}(a(h))\bigr).$$
The four maps are those named in [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]: the etale adjunction transported by the compact-support comparison and the full faithfulness of $\nu_X^*$ on $D^+$. This just writes the four specified maps on a morphism; it does not identify an arbitrary natural bijection with the specified one. The witness map is $1_{S_XG}$, so precomposition with its inverse contributes an identity.

source.place: four-factor relative Hom construction and final paragraph on compactification comparisons

proof.text:
Put $h=g\circ q_{S_XG}$, $t=g\circ B_G:S_YFG\to M$, and $v=U_Y(t)\circ\eta_{Y,FG}:FG\to N$. The definition of $B_G$ and cancellation of $S_Y(e_G^{-1})$ with $S_Y(e_G)$ give
$$h\circ C_{c,G}^{-1}=t\circ S_Y(e_G).$$
Naturality of the actual unit of $S_Y\dashv U_Y$ at $e_G:F_cG\to FG$ says
$$U_YS_Y(e_G)\circ\eta_{Y,F_cG}=\eta_{Y,FG}\circ e_G.$$
Apply $U_Y$ to the first equality and use the second to obtain
$$a(h)=U_Y(t)\circ U_YS_Y(e_G)\circ\eta_{Y,F_cG}=v\circ e_G.$$
Thus $a(h)\circ e_G^{-1}=v$, with the source $FG$ retained throughout.

source.place: four-factor relative Hom construction and final paragraph on compactification comparisons

proof.text:
For any $a:F_cG\to N$, put $x=\beta^c_{G,N}(a):G\to I_cN$. The inverse Hom map of an adjunction sends $x$ to its left-adjoint image followed by the counit, so $\varepsilon^c_N\circ F_c(x)=a$. The counit equation for $r$ is the counit identity of the conjugate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] of $\tau=e^{-1}:F\to F_c$: where $\eta^F$ is the unit of $F\dashv I$ and $r_N=I(\varepsilon^c_N)\circ I(e^{-1}_{I_cN})\circ\eta^F_{I_cN}$, naturality of $\varepsilon$ and the triangle identity $\varepsilon_{FI_cN}\circ F(\eta^F_{I_cN})=1$ give $\varepsilon_N\circ F(r_N)=\varepsilon^c_N\circ e^{-1}_{I_cN}$. Compute the inverse $\beta$-transpose of $r_N\circ x$ using this counit equation (the one displayed in the statement) and naturality of $e^{-1}$ at $x$:
$$\begin{aligned}
\varepsilon_N\circ F(r_N\circ x)
&=\varepsilon^c_N\circ e_{I_cN}^{-1}\circ F(x)\\
&=\varepsilon^c_N\circ F_c(x)\circ e_G^{-1}\\
&=a\circ e_G^{-1}.
\end{aligned}$$
Applying the bijection $\beta_{G,N}$ proves
$$r_N\circ\beta^c_{G,N}(a)=\beta_{G,N}(a\circ e_G^{-1}).$$
All equalities follow from the two given adjunctions, their defining inverse transpose formula, and the displayed counit compatibility; no separate uniqueness or change-of-adjoint theorem is needed.

source.place: four-factor relative Hom construction and final paragraph on compactification comparisons

proof.text:
Apply the calculation of step 4 to $a=a(h)$ from steps 2 and 3. Since $a(h)e_G^{-1}=v$, functoriality of $S_X$ gives
$$\begin{aligned}
S_X(r_N)\circ\Phi^c_{G,M}(g\circ q_{S_XG})
&=S_X\bigl(r_N\circ\beta^c_{G,N}(a(h))\bigr)\\
&=S_X\bigl(\beta_{G,N}(v)\bigr)\\
&=S_X\!\left(\beta_{G,U_YM}\!\left(U_Y(g\circ B_G)\circ\eta_{Y,FG}\right)\right).
\end{aligned}$$
This is the required equality. Each of the four maps is natural: $B$ is a composite of the given natural isomorphisms, the next two maps are the natural Hom maps of the specified adjunctions, and the fourth is a functor's Hom map. Their bijectivity was checked in step 1. The same calculation applies to every displayed $G,M,g$, so it identifies the specified natural Hom bijections. The identity witness contributes only the identity map from step 2.
